themes_detail.label: Cannabis Retailer Surge
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints spiked to 6 this week versus a baseline of 1.0 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 500% increase (z-score: 7.07)—signaling either rapid illegal retail expansion or enforcement gaps in Greenwich Village/SoHo this week.
evidence: 6 cannabis retailer complaints this week vs. 1.0 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 7.07 indicates statistically extreme spike
500% increase suggests emerging or accelerating unlicensed retail activity
reporting_angles: Investigate whether complaints reflect unlicensed vs. licensed retailers; interview NYPD enforcement or cannabis regulatory board
Canvass Spring Street and surrounding commercial corridors to identify specific retail locations and map against recent 311 heat map
Interview residents and business owners about neighborhood perception of cannabis retail growth and quality-of-life impacts

themes_detail.label: Dead/Dying Street Trees
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints jumped to 3 this week, a 700% spike from a baseline of 0.4 per week over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.42), and aligns with recurring community board budget requests for forestry services—suggesting a maintenance gap worsening now.
evidence: 3 dead/dying tree complaints this week vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 5.42 indicates statistically significant spike
Community board has requested forestry services and tree maintenance funding year-over-year, indicating chronic underfunding
reporting_angles: Request Parks Department canopy assessment data for CD 102; verify whether this week's spike reflects recent storm damage or deferred maintenance
Photograph and geolocate the specific trees triggering complaints this week; interview Parks Department on response timelines
Frame as failure of recurring budget request: community asked for tree maintenance funding repeatedly, and now trees are dying

themes_detail.label: Illegal Parking Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal parking complaints hit 126 two weeks ago, a 69% jump from the 8-week baseline of 74.8 per week (z-score: 4.86), indicating sustained pressure on street enforcement that persists into the current reporting period.
evidence: 126 illegal parking complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 74.8 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks
Illegal parking is top complaint type overall (1,082 in 90 days), indicating persistent baseline problem
reporting_angles: Check Sanitation and NYPD enforcement activity 2 weeks ago; was there a staffing gap or holiday impact?
Interview parking permit holders and residents about specific corridors with worst violations (e.g., Spring Street, University Place)
Assess whether this is tied to construction debris permits or temporary loading restrictions from ongoing ULURP/DOB activity

themes_detail.label: Rodent Activity Escalation
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints spiked to 11 two weeks ago, a 238% increase from the 3.2 weekly baseline (z-score: 3.91), coinciding with elevated unsanitary condition complaints (30 complaints 3 weeks ago, up 126%) and suggesting a sanitation or structural decay cluster.
evidence: 11 rodent complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 3.2 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks
Unsanitary condition complaints (30) peaked 3 weeks ago at 126% above baseline, suggesting linked environmental degradation
reporting_angles: Request detailed 311 complaint geo-data to identify specific blocks or buildings triggering rodent clusters; cross-reference with HPD housing violation history
Interview Sanitation on collection frequency and catch basin cleaning (community board requested catch basin cleaning for years)
Frame as convergence story: recurring budget requests for sanitation equipment and housing inspections have not been fully funded, leading to deterioration

themes_detail.label: Paint/Plaster Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Paint and plaster complaints jumped to 19 three weeks ago, a 134% increase from the 8.1 weekly baseline (z-score: 3.88), signaling accelerated building exterior decay across the district—likely tied to deferred HPD housing inspections and code enforcement.
evidence: 19 paint/plaster complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 8.1 weekly baseline over prior 8 weeks
Community board has requested 'housing inspections to correct code violations' funding year-over-year
reporting_angles: Request HPD data on open violations and inspection wait times for CD 102; assess capacity vs. complaint volume
Photograph visible exterior deterioration on SoHo and Greenwich Village blocks; tie to specific buildings with long violation histories
Interview HPD and CB about why recurring requests for housing inspection funding have not been fulfilled, and what threshold of complaints triggers enforcement action
